class_name FrameScheduler
extends RefCounted

# Frame-Based Cooperative Coroutine Scheduler
# --------------------------------------------

var current_frame: int = 0

enum WaitType { FRAMES, UNTIL, SIGNAL }

class Task:
    var id: int
    var name: String
    var co: GDScriptFunctionState
    var on_complete: Callable
    var wait_type: WaitType
    var wait_frames: int
    var wait_until: Callable
    var wait_signal: Signal
    var signal_emitted: bool = false

var _tasks: Array[Task] = []
var _next_id: int = 0

func spawn(task_name: String, body: Callable, on_complete: Callable = Callable()) -> void:
    var task := Task.new()
    task.id = _next_id
    _next_id += 1
    task.name = task_name
    task.on_complete = on_complete
    # Start synchronously until first suspension or completion
    task.co = body.call()
    if not (task.co is GDScriptFunctionState):
        # Already finished, but the problem says tasks suspend.
        # This handles a body that doesn't suspend at all.
        if task.on_complete.is_valid():
            task.on_complete.call(task.name)
        return
    _tasks.append(task)

func wait_frames(n: int) -> void:
    var frame := current_frame
    yield_control(WaitType.FRAMES, frame + n)

func wait_until(cond: Callable) -> void:
    yield_control(WaitType.UNTIL, 0, cond)

func wait_signal(sig: Signal) -> void:
    var task := _find_current_task()
    task.signal_emitted = false
    # Connect once, permanently; task.signal_emitted tracks emission.
    sig.connect(_on_signal.bind(task), CONNECT_PERSISTENT)
    yield_control(WaitType.SIGNAL, 0, Callable(), sig)

func _on_signal(task: Task) -> void:
    task.signal_emitted = true

func _find_current_task() -> Task:
    # The task at the front of _tasks is the one currently running, 
    # because spawn suspends it to the front, and advance keeps only pending.
    # But wait_* calls are in the body, so the current task is the front-most
    # one that just called yield_control.
    if _tasks.is_empty():
        return null
    return _tasks[0]

func yield_control(type: WaitType, frame: int = 0, cond: Callable = Callable(), sig: Signal = Signal()) -> void:
    var task := _find_current_task()
    task.wait_type = type
    task.wait_frames = frame
    task.wait_until = cond
    task.wait_signal = sig
    # Resume the main resume loop that called the body
    task.co.resume()

func advance(frames: int) -> void:
    for _f in range(frames):
        current_frame += 1
        # Re-consider all not-yet-finished, currently-suspended tasks once in task-id order.
        # Collect current tasks first so those that suspend again aren't reconsidered this frame.
        var snapshot := _tasks.duplicate()
        _tasks.clear()
        for task in snapshot:
            var ready := false
            match task.wait_type:
                WaitType.FRAMES:
                    if task.wait_frames == current_frame:
                        ready = true
                WaitType.UNTIL:
                    if task.wait_until.is_valid() and task.wait_until.call():
                        ready = true
                WaitType.SIGNAL:
                    if task.signal_emitted:
                        ready = true
            
            if ready:
                # Resume synchronously until next suspension or completion
                var next_res := task.co.resume()
                if not (next_res is GDScriptFunctionState):
                    # Task finished, run callback immediately
                    if task.on_complete.is_valid():
                        task.on_complete.call(task.name)
                else:
                    # Re-suspend, task already has new wait info from its body
                    _tasks.append(task)
            else:
                # Stay suspended, same wait condition
                _tasks.append(task)
